attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The proof still lacks a Yang-Mills construction of the amplification parameter and the factorization q(t)=e^{t h} inside the locked nonabelian Wilson algebra; trace products may decompose into representations with extra self-intersection or boundary renormalizations.
steps: Start with cutoff reflection positivity: Q_{a,L}(F,c)=\sum\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i,F_j)\ge0 for collar-supported Wilson observables.
Use RG convergence valid for reflected collar probes to pass to continuum fixed-collar matrices N^{\delta}\ge0 by the closed-cone argument.
Let \delta\downarrow0. Diagonal trace continuity plus positivity kills positive additive contact matrices, so any remaining obstruction is multiplicative: N=B\circ M.
Normalize diagonals to get the intended target quotient q=\widehat M=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B. The same-theory problem is exactly q\ge0 on every realized finite Wilson block.

Instead of requiring quotient phases to be coboundaries, choose the collar-continuous Hermitian logarithm h=Log q. If h is conditionally positive on zero-sum vectors, Schoenberg gives e^{h}=q\ge0; hence the target block is OS positive.
If the Wilson algebra realizes q(t)=e^{t h} through same-theory amplification, positivity of q(t) for small t forces h to be conditionally positive by differentiating z^*q(t)z on z\perp1.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: Log-CPD is a clean finite matrix certificate, but we have not shown that the continuum RG bounds compute h, that h is CPD for Yang-Mills hairpins, or that the required logarithmic branch and nonzero entries are valid for all dense Wilson blocks.

assumptions: For each finite family W_i, the fixed-collar matrices converge to a positive matrix N.
Diagonal trace continuity eliminates positive additive contacts; any remaining boundary anomaly is multiplicative and nonzero on the block.
The normalized intended target block is q=\widehat N\oslash \widehat B with q_{ii}=1 and q_{ji}=\overline{q_{ij}}.
A continuous Hermitian logarithm h_{ij}=\operatorname{Log} q_{ij}, h_{ii}=0, is selected by the collar deformation.
h is conditionally positive: \sum_{i,j}\overline z_i z_j h_{ij}\ge0 whenever \sum_i z_i=0.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive gauge-invariant Schwinger forms S_{a,L} on a locked Wilson/local observable core, with collar supports t\ge \delta and RG convergence for all reflected finite pairings.
target object: continuum OS-positive Schwinger functions on the same gauge-invariant observable core, with the intended reflection-plane Wilson limits and no added boundary degrees of freedom.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, first by fixed-collar closed-cone transfer and then by a finite Schur quotient across the collar trace.

same-theory condition: the collar-to-plane map identifies each Wilson observable with its predeclared continuum renormalization; multiplicative boundary factors may only be divided out if the resulting quotient matrix is positive on the realized locked algebra, not by changing the algebra.

equations.label: multiplicative boundary quotient
equations.valid_when: Additive boundary contacts have vanished and B_{ij}\ne0 on the finite Wilson block.

equations.label: log-Schoenberg certificate
equations.valid_when: The logarithm is Hermitian on the chosen branch; this is the complex Schoenberg theorem for normalized positive kernels.

equations.label: three-point determinant test
equations.valid_when: q is a normalized 3 by 3 quotient block; failure is a direct OS falsifier for that realized triple.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a realized Wilson block with q not PSD, or under valid amplification find z with \sum z_i=0 and z^*\operatorname{Log}(q)z<0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Replaces a phase-coboundary heuristic by a finite logarithmic kernel criterion; sufficient for each block and exact if the locked algebra realizes continuous boundary amplifications.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For any finite locked Wilson hairpin block, after fixed-collar OS positivity and after additive boundary contacts vanish, the same-theory target OS matrix is positive if its normalized boundary quotient q has a Hermitian logarithm h=Log q that is conditionally positive on the zero-sum subspace. This complex log-CPD test is a valid Schoenberg certificate and strictly sharpens the previous coboundary-phase plus CND-modulus sufficient condition.

assumptions: q(t) is the normalized Schur quotient for actual observables in the locked algebra, not an adjoined formal matrix.
q(0)=J and q(t) is OS positive for all sufficiently small t>0.
q(t)=e^{t h+o(t)} entrywise with a Hermitian first variation.
definitions: amplification parameter: a same-theory operation such as replicated thin hairpins or a Poissonized Wilson insertion whose boundary quotient exponentiates entrywise.
zero-sum test vector: a vector z with \sum_i z_i=0, so the rank-one limit J has z^*Jz=0.
log generator: h_{ij}=\partial_t q_{ij}(t)|_{t=0}, Hermitian with h_{ii}=0.

equations.label: infinitesimal zero-sum test
equations.valid_when: q(0)=J and q(t) has the stated entrywise logarithmic derivative.

equations.label: necessity of log-CPD
equations.valid_when: The amplified quotient matrices are valid OS matrices of the same theory.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A negative zero-sum logarithmic quadratic form is a small-t falsifier of same-theory amplification even if the unamplified q at t=1 happens to be PSD.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns log-CPD from a sufficient certificate into a necessary condition once amplification closure is proved.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the locked Wilson core realizes a collar amplification parameter t with quotient blocks q(t)=\exp(t h) for t in a neighborhood of 0, then same-theory OS positivity for all amplified observables forces h to be conditionally positive on the zero-sum subspace.

assumptions: The branch of \log |q_{ij}| is fixed by collar continuity.
d is CND on every finite realized Wilson block.
definitions: phase coboundary: \arg q_{ij}=\alpha_i-\alpha_j, equivalently all triangle phase holonomies vanish modulo the chosen branch.
CND modulus: d_{ij}=-\log |q_{ij}|, d_{ii}=0, and \sum\overline z_i z_j d_{ij}\le0 for every zero-sum z.
diagonal unitary removal: q=D e^{-d}D^*, D_{ii}=e^{i\alpha_i}.

equations.label: coboundary reduction
equations.valid_when: The quotient phase has zero cycle holonomy on the support graph.

equations.label: Schoenberg real modulus
equations.valid_when: d_{ii}=0 and d is conditionally negative definite on finite blocks.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Nonzero triangle holonomy is not by itself a falsifier after this correction; it becomes one only if the full determinant or log-CPD test fails.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Gives an easily checkable sufficient route, but not the exact obstruction when nontrivial magnetic phase is dominated by the real part of h.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The old phase-coboundary plus CND-modulus condition is a transparent sufficient case of log-CPD: if q_{ij}=e^{i(\alpha_i-\alpha_j)}e^{-d_{ij}} and d is conditionally negative definite, then q is PSD and all Schur powers q^{\circ t} are PSD.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if Wilson amplification cannot be formulated in the locked gauge-invariant algebra or if boundary logarithms generically have zeros/branch jumps.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves that reflected Wilson boundary quotients have a Hermitian log-CPD generator on a dense core, with RG estimates validating the collar OPE.
control_decision.reason: The branch gained a sharper bridge lemma and avoided an overclaim about phase holonomy. The remaining work is a concrete boundary OPE/amplification calculation, not another abstract topology definition.

dependency_updates.description: The formal fixed-collar closed-cone step remains valid; the post-collar step is now a finite log-CPD Schur quotient problem.
Must audit whether the locked Wilson algebra is closed under the amplification operations needed to make log-CPD necessary, without changing the theory.
Besides convergence of reflected quadratic forms, the topology must control boundary OPE limits defining B and h on finite Wilson blocks.

falsifiers: Direct finite falsifier: a realized three-hairpin quotient with 1+2Re(q12 q23 conjugate(q13))-|q12|^2-|q23|^2-|q13|^2<0.
Infinitesimal falsifier: an amplified family with z^*Log(q)z<0 for some zero-sum z, giving negative OS norm for small amplification t.
Branch falsifier: zeros of B or q appear in the collar limit, so the logarithmic Schur quotient is not a same-theory boundary trace but a boundary superselection collapse.
Algebra falsifier: replicated or Poissonized hairpins require adding observables or boundary counterterms not present in the original gauge-invariant test algebra.
Topology falsifier: RG convergence remains valid for fixed collars but not for the logarithmic boundary OPE needed to identify h.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 207 corrects and sharpens the previous two-stage obstruction. Vanishing triangle phase holonomy plus CND modulus is a useful sufficient certificate, but the more intrinsic finite bridge is complex logarithmic conditional positivity of q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B. Nonzero phase holonomy is therefore not automatically a falsifier; it is detected through the full determinant or log-CPD quadratic form. If same-theory Wilson amplifications are valid, log-CPD becomes necessary by an infinitesimal zero-sum test.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the reflected three-hairpin boundary quotient to first nontrivial order, extract h=Log q, and test z^*hz on the two-dimensional zero-sum subspace; compare with the determinant falsifier at t=1.

Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
